title: Priority synthesis and evidence collector for multi-jurisdiction security requests
creator: Maya Chen
description: Customers frequently open distinct security/compliance asks (SOC2, ISO, HIPAA, GDPR/DPA, vendor questionnaires) that require different evidence artifacts and different priority servicing. This ticket scopes a product-led solution: a single intake synthesizer that normalizes incoming asks, scores requests by business/risk urgency, and automatically assembles an evidence bundle (where available) for faster triage and response. The goal is to reduce manual work in Support/Security, improve SLA predictability for enterprise onboarding, and surface repeatable gaps our product/infra teams can remediate.
context: We currently route most enterprise security requests via a manual Slack/Sheets pipeline and ad-hoc Confluence links. This leads to: long response times on complex questionnaires, duplicated evidence collection work across deals, and poor prioritization when legal/regulatory timelines conflict with technical constraints. Several recent deals (multi-region healthcare and EU financial customers) stalled because evidence collection took weeks. We need an intake-first system that codifies ask types and returns a ready-to-send evidence package or a clear remediation checklist.
goals: Define a normalized schema for incoming security/compliance questions (question -> canonical requirement mapping)
Build a scoring model to prioritize requests by revenue impact, regulatory timeline, and technical remediation effort
Implement an evidence collector that can attach existing artifacts (SOC2 report, encryption design, DPA template, HIPAA BAAs) and flag gaps with templated remediation guidance
Expose a lightweight PM dashboard to track SLA, aging, and recurring evidence gaps
Reduce average time-to-first-response for high-priority enterprise security asks to <48 hours
success_metrics: Average time-to-first-response for P0/P1 requests decreases from 7 days to <48 hours
Percent of incoming vendor/customer questionnaires with automated evidence bundle >= 40% within quarter
Number of unique evidence artifacts reused across >3 deals increases by 3x
Support/Security reported manual assembly time per questionnaire drops by >= 60%
acceptance_criteria: Accepts incoming requests from existing intake channels (Support form, enterprise onboarding form, direct remap from Slack) and normalizes into canonical schema
Priority scoring algorithm implemented and surfaced on ticket with rationale breakdown (revenue, jurisdiction urgency, technical effort)
Evidence collector can match and attach at least 6 common artifacts (SOC2 attestation, ISO summary, DPA template, encryption spec, data residency statement, SOC2 gap log) from the documents store
When artifacts are missing, system produces a templated remediation checklist and assigns an owner or request to the appropriate engineering backlog
Dashboard shows SLA, queue depth by priority, and top 10 recurring missing artifacts
Security team has reviewed the retention/access model for evidence bundles and approved the read/access controls
architecture_notes: High-level approach: a lightweight ingestion service will parse questionnaire metadata (source, jurisdiction, legal deadline, required standards) and run rules + ML-based mapping to canonical requirements. Evidence collector will query a document store keyed by canonical requirement and match via metadata + semantic search. A scoring function (configurable weights) will compute priority. Minimal UI: a compact intake review page in Console and an exportable evidence bundle attachment for email/Drive upload.
risks: Overfitting the canonical schema to current questionnaires; future vendor forms may introduce new fields
Access control for evidence bundles must be tightly restricted or we risk leaking sensitive attestations
Automated matches may create false positives; legal needs final sign-off before sending to customers
Underestimating engineering effort to integrate with dispersed document stores and existing Confluence/Drive artifacts
